chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Is ibn al-Qasim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who missed a night from the nights of Mina. He said: There is no penalty upon him, but he has done poorly.

key_terms.أَسَاءَ: He did poorly / committed a shortcoming
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: There is no penalty/obligation upon him
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a valley near Mecca where pilgrims stay during Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim misses a night in Mina during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Isfahani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that missing a single night of stay in Mina incurs no financial penalty (dam), yet the pilgrim is still considered to have committed a minor shortcoming (aqsara). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between obligatory acts whose omission requires compensation and those where the omission is merely a spiritual or ritual deficiency without material cost. The context underscores the flexibility in Hajj rituals, allowing for the combination of stays in Mina and Mecca under certain conditions.
